page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the t2a server family. It is powered by an Ampere Altra processor utilizing the arm64 architecture, specifically featuring 32 dedicated physical cores based on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. Operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz, each core runs a single thread, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The instance is configured with 128 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations position the t2a-standard-32 in the average performance tier for most multi-core and memory operations. The instance achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 58004.62 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12780.0. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 2259.49 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 165.27 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core scores of 1086.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression of 8.63 GB/sec falling into the weaker percentiles.

This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for scale-out workloads that benefit from high physical core density and dedicated CPU allocation without hyperthreading. It is well-suited for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, static web serving with 30.04 GB/sec throughput, and database operations like Redis, which registers 40.8 million SET operations per second. Conversely, it is poorly suited for large-scale LLM inference, where text generation speeds drop to 2.31 tokens/sec for 70B models, and other single-thread intensive applications.

Operating without hyperthreading, it provides a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place the instance in the average tier for multi-threaded workloads, demonstrating a stress-ng multi-core score of 58004.62 and a static web serving throughput of 30.04 GB/sec. However, single-core performance presents a tradeoff, as evidenced by a lower Geekbench single-core score of 1086.0. This instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out, multi-threaded applications such as software compilation, web serving, and database operations, while being less optimal for single-threaded tasks or large-scale language model inference.
